items.title: World War I Unit Bundle
items.summary: A complete U.S. History unit on World War I for grades 9-12.
items.description:
World War I Unit Bundle is a complete U.S. History unit for grades 9-12. The cover marks it for South Carolina USHC Standard 4.

Nine lessons follow the war from the 1914 spark that pulled Europe in, through the United States trying to stay out, to how the government persuaded Americans to support the war. One lesson is a mission briefing on how the war started. Lesson 4, Selling the War: Propaganda and the Press, asks how that message was built. Students judge the choice later in the unit.

The bundle includes nine lessons, an 8-bit slide deck and a plain-font slide deck, student packets, answer keys, a DBQ, a unit test, and a study guide. The files are Google Docs and Google Slides.

Griffin & Quill is a Teachers Pay Teachers Exclusive Seller. This site does not take payment. Buy on TPT opens this unit on Teachers Pay Teachers.

items.title: World War II Unit Bundle
items.summary: A complete U.S. History unit on World War II for grades 9-12.
items.description:
World War II Unit Bundle is a complete U.S. History unit for grades 9-12. The cover marks it for South Carolina USHC Standard 4.

Nine lessons follow the United States from trying to stay out of another war in the 1930s through the attack on Pearl Harbor. Lesson 1, Peace at Any Price? Dictators, Neutrality and America, 1931-1939, asks why staying out was so hard. A later checkpoint uses a photograph of the USS Arizona on December 7, 1941, and asks students what they see, what listeners would need to know, and to write a headline.

The bundle includes nine lessons, an 8-bit slide deck and a plain-font slide deck, student packets, a DBQ, a unit test, and a study guide. The files are Google Docs and Google Slides. The cover also lists real historical images and nine unique activities.

Griffin & Quill is a Teachers Pay Teachers Exclusive Seller. This site does not take payment. Buy on TPT opens this unit on Teachers Pay Teachers.
